subject: Private deployment: Operator-escrow lite & sovereign hosting rider
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medtech.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: David Park <david.park@medtech.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — operator access & sovereign hosting rider

Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving ahead with the POC on our internal dev cluster but legal asked us to get a little more prescriptive on the follow points before we execute the Order Form + addendum:

- We need a "sovereign hosting rider" that restricts data residency to our US-only region and confirms no cross-border replication.
- Operator access: we need an "escrow-lite" approach — a short, auditable playbook showing how Redwood would provide operator interventions, and an evidence delivery option if support access is required during an audit.
- Clarify custody of symmetric keys used for snapshot exports (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed).

Can you loop in legal? We'd like a redline we can circulate to our counsel by EOD Wednesday.

Regards,
Sarah Liu
Head of Procurement, MedTech Systems

Cc: David Park <david.park@medtech.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — operator access & sovereign hosting rider

Sarah — thanks, and congrats on getting internal approval to POC. Looping in Laura from Legal.

Immediate plan:
- Laura will propose a compact rider that addresses residency, operator intervention constraints, and key custody.
- I will draft an "escrow-lite" technical appendix describing the evidence package and access controls (what we can show, how we sanitize logs, time windows).
- We have an internal template for customer-managed KMS and a fallback for Redwood-held envelope keys — I'll include both options.

Can you confirm the audit frequency expectation (annual vs triggered) and whether the evidence needs to be delivered to your internal legal team or a third‑party auditor?

I aim to have a first draft to you by EOD Wednesday.

— Priyom

Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medtech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — operator access & sovereign hosting rider

Sarah / Priyom — attaching a proposed rider and a brief redline that covers the three asks. Key notes from legal:
- License scope: we maintain the standard MSA license grant for the model runtime; the rider will add an explicit non-transfer/host-only clause for on‑prem/VPC deployments so there's no implication of additional redistribution rights.
- Operator interventions: we can agree to an "operator evidence delivery" mechanism limited to (i) a short window (48 hours) of remote troubleshooting with customer authorization and (ii) a written attestation of actions taken. We will not give remote shell access to MedTech-owned environments without a signed exception.
- Key custody: we prefer customer-managed KMS; if customer chooses Redwood escrow for keys, we require an escrow protocol (sealed envelope + dual-control) and a quarterly rotation/attestation.

Open items for your counsel: the proposed language allows Redwood to ship a read-only snapshot of operational logs and redacted runtime state for audit. Your team should confirm whether an encrypted disk image is acceptable vs a parsed evidentiary bundle.

Attachments: Proposed_Rider_v1.docx; MedTech_Redlines_20260630.pdf

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: contracts@jonesco-law.com <contracts@jonesco-law.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medtech.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment — redlines to proposed rider

Laura/Sarah — thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from MedTech counsel: 
1) They want the evidence delivery to be via a documented chain-of-custody and prefer a hashed disk image (SHA256) delivered on encrypted transfer, with Redwood providing a verification log.
2) Operator intervention: request to limit Redwood's ability to access customer environments to read-only unless a separate custom SOW is executed; they want a one-time emergency access clause with dual approval (customer security + MedTech legal).
3) Key custody: they will accept Redwood escrow only if a neutral third-party escrow agent is named and the release conditions are narrowly tailored (e.g., insolvency, failure to support).

We've annotated MedTech_Redlines_20260630.pdf and uploaded comments to your Drive folder. We can do a quick call tomorrow to resolve the release conditions.

Best,
Jones & Co. — Contracts Team
